description: Hi, I'm Ved, an engineering student working on drone/UAV systems. We're building the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser: a web tool to compare lunar south pole landing sites and dates by visualizing Sun and Earth positions vs. the horizon. Looking for: frontend dev (React/JS), data viz (D3/Three.js), Python for ephemerides (SpiceyPy/Astropy), and UI/UX or video skills. Fully virtual, beginners welcome!
summary:
LUNA-SCOPE is a lunar landing-site exploration and mission-planning platform focused on the Moon's south pole. It brings terrain information, Sun and Earth geometry, solar illumination, communication visibility and mission-level comparison into one interactive workflow.

Using NASA lunar data and space-science resources, the prototype helps users examine candidate regions such as Shackleton Rim, de Gerlache Rim and Malapert Massif, explore operational trade-offs over time, and understand the evidence and uncertainty behind each result.

Our goal is to make complex lunar landing-site analysis easier to explore, understand and compare—not to certify a site as safe.
details:
Project Overview

Choosing a lunar landing site is a multi-factor problem. A location must be evaluated not only for its terrain, but also for its local horizon, solar access and ability to communicate with Earth. These conditions change with location and time, making it difficult to understand the complete operational picture using isolated tools.

LUNA-SCOPE brings these considerations into one interactive environment.

How it works

1. Terrain Analysis

The platform uses NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation products to study lunar terrain. It processes elevation, slope, roughness and terrain-quality information to identify preliminary hazards and understand the limitations of the available data.

2. Sun and Earth Geometry

The celestial analysis workflow uses SPICE/NAIF and NASA JPL Horizons resources to examine the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to selected lunar locations.

3. Solar and Communication Analysis

The platform evaluates time-dependent solar illumination and Earth visibility. The Operations Timeline brings these conditions together and preserves unresolved intervals rather than assuming that missing information means visibility is available.

4. Mission Intelligence

The Mission Intelligence engine supports mission profiles, feasibility checks, weighted comparisons and scenario summaries for candidate landing locations.

5. AI Mission Copilot

The Copilot provides a natural-language interface to the project's scientific tools. It helps users navigate terrain information, mission assessments and site comparisons. The current implementation uses deterministic question routing rather than a live large language model.

Why it matters

LUNA-SCOPE aims to make complex lunar site analysis easier to understand and compare. By bringing terrain, illumination, communication and mission considerations together, it can help identify operational trade-offs and areas where further scientific investigation is needed.

The current system is a research and hackathon prototype. Some Mission Intelligence example assessments use synthetic fixtures and must not be interpreted as NASA-derived rankings or validated landing probabilities. The system is not a landing-safety certification tool.

Technology

  • Python and scientific/geospatial processing
  • FastAPI backend
  • React and TypeScript frontend
  • Browser-based 3D visualization
  • SPICE/SpiceyPy
  • NASA JPL Horizons
  • NASA LOLA terrain products
  • Automated unit, integration and scientific regression testing
